method: Alice's lesson today revolved around ml5.js, a machine learning library that utilizes P5.js. I followed along with her examples on screen as well as following along with the getting started page on the website. It was a bit tricky as there were a few moments where the program would freeze when I expected it to show emojis on the fingers it was tracking, but I was able to get it working and to have it track the points on my hands, and to place things on those hands in the program.
related_work: This week was mainly finishing the example projects and remaking them myself. Through these projects I got a better idea of how networking worked with P5.js, and how to setup a networked project that I could share with my friends and experience together.
title: More P5.js education, ml5.js
introduction: This week was a bit of a catchup week for me, as I wanted to complete the week 5 project example, recreating that as well as the week 6 one, but I also learned how to use ml5.js.
